query:
Research public X posts about building trustworthy, maintainable LLM-assisted
technical/scientific knowledge wikis. The decision is whether exhaustive reading
of all bundled documents/source code should be a prerequisite to a useful wiki,
or whether scoped question/claim-based verification can work. Seek counterexamples,
not agreement. Use actual X search. Return only posts with exact canonical X
status URLs, author, publication date, a concise paraphrase, any linked original
repository/paper, and whether it is first-hand implementation, proposal, measured
evaluation, criticism, or promotion. Do not invent posts, quotes, measurements,
or imply search results represent all users. No verbatim quote over 20 words per
author. Distinguish author claims from verified facts and your inference.
Do not give popularity rankings. If no matching evidence exists, say so.

Verify only these three candidate X posts, using the X index and per-post tool
citations: https://x.com/karpathy/status/2041162213160091996 ,
https://x.com/thenightshipper/status/2089638769653883208 ,
https://x.com/mohitmor_ai/status/2043363748174508364 .
For each, state whether the exact post was actually retrieved, give its date and
an evidence-faithful paraphrase. Specifically test whether Karpathy says the wiki
approach skips writing but does not skip reading/thinking; whether Kothari discusses
loss of raw-source provenance; whether Mor discusses token cost of upkeep.
Do not reuse previous summaries as evidence. Do not cite unrelated posts to support
these. No population-level claims or policy recommendation. If inaccessible, mark
that candidate unverified. Every retrieved item must have its own X tool citation.
answer:
**Verified candidate 1**  
**Canonical URL**: https://x.com/karpathy/status/2041162213160091996  
**Author**: Andrej Karpathy (@karpathy)  
**Publication date**: April 6, 2026  
**Retrieved**: Yes, via direct fetch of the exact post ID.[[1]](https://x.com/i/status/2041162213160091996)

**Concise paraphrase**: The author claims the LLM wiki method skips manual writing of the knowledge base but still requires the user to read source material, LLM summaries, and analyses of how new content fits the existing structure; the author states this combination works in his experience and that the balance of reading versus LLM assistance is flexible per document.[[1]](https://x.com/i/status/2041162213160091996)

**Linked original repository/paper**: None in this specific post.  
**Type**: Explanation accompanying first-hand implementation.  

**Specific test**: The exact retrieved post confirms that Karpathy states the wiki approach skips writing but does not skip reading/thinking. This is the author's claim; the retrieval itself is the verified fact. No inference is supplied beyond the post content.

**Verified candidate 2**  
**Canonical URL**: https://x.com/thenightshipper/status/2089638769653883208  
**Author**: Abhishek Kothari (@thenightshipper)  
**Publication date**: August 18, 2026  
**Retrieved**: Yes, via direct fetch of the exact post ID.[[2]](https://x.com/i/status/2089638769653883208)

**Concise paraphrase**: The author claims that both large LLM-generated wikis and similar projects eventually produce derived pages that cite other derived pages, causing claims to lose any traceable link to original raw sources; the author calls this a data swamp and states that explicit lineage tracking is required so any claim can be traced to its upstream raw source and any subsequent changes.[[2]](https://x.com/i/status/2089638769653883208)

**Linked original repository/paper**: None in this specific post.  
**Type**: Criticism.  

**Specific test**: The exact retrieved post confirms that Kothari discusses loss of raw-source provenance. This is the author's claim; the retrieval itself is the verified fact. No inference is supplied beyond the post content.

**Verified candidate 3**  
**Canonical URL**: https://x.com/mohitmor_ai/status/2043363748174508364  
**Author**: Mohit Mor (@mohitmor_ai)  
**Publication date**: April 12, 2026  
**Retrieved**: Yes, via direct fetch of the exact post ID.[[3]](https://x.com/i/status/2043363748174508364)

**Concise paraphrase**: The author claims that LLM-wiki extension ideas look promising in theory but fail to account for token costs of maintaining detailed designs and structures; the author states that optimizing for token-cost reduction makes real implementations diverge from the theoretical versions.[[3]](https://x.com/i/status/2043363748174508364)

**Linked original repository/paper**: None in this specific post.  
**Type**: Criticism.  

**Specific test**: The exact retrieved post confirms that Mor discusses token cost of upkeep. This is the author's claim; the retrieval itself is the verified fact. No inference is supplied beyond the post content.
